Ezechias 4. lib. Reg cap. 20. gravi morbo conflic-
tatus, convertit faciem suam ad parietem & oravit
Dominum: tunc dixit Dominus, audivi orationem
tuam, & vidi lachrymam tuam: & ecce sanavi te, die
tertio ascendes templu Domini. Deinde dixit Esaias,
asse te massam ficorum. Quam cum attulissent, &
posuissent super hulcus
ejus, curatus est.
Hunc ordinem omnes ægroti servent, primum o-
rent Dominum: deinde medicamenta adhibeant.
Duæ: Pathologice, Die erforschung der Krankheit;
Et Therapeutice, Die Artzneyung der Kranckheit.
Est prima pars Medicinæ de morbis investigandis.
Morbus est affectus corporis præter naturam, à quo
vitiatur actio.
Morbi duo præcipua vulgò dicuntur signa: urina
& pulsus. Sed Dominus Doctor Scribonius acriter
invehitur in eos, qui ex qualibet urina de quolibet
morbo judicare volunt, & ostendit multis rationi-
bus, inutilem & vanam esse illorum doctrinam, qui
contendunt, omnes morbos & affectiones interiores
humani corporis ex aspectu urinarum observari &
videri posse, in libello de idea Medicinæ, Lemgoviæ
excuso.
Pulsus est motus cordis
& arteriarum. Pulsum ex-
plorant medici missa manu in carpum.
Duplex: Aut enim est ex intemperie, aut ex mala con-
formatione: Cuius species est continui solutio. Intem-

page.notes: Reading of the first word of the page is doubtful because the left edge is damaged; the initial letter is cut off. The word "ejus" is printed "cjus" and is read as ejus. "hulcus" is kept as printed. The German black-letter words are transcribed as I read them; "Krankheit" and "Kranckheit" are the printed forms as far as legible. The final word "sicca" is printed with a letter that looks like f; read as sicca.
